{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts (repeat):
- When sending a PUT to update an entry, the description field has three distinct meanings:
  1) description omitted (field absent from the JSON) means: do NOT modify the stored description on the server.
  2) description present with JSON null means: clear the stored description (set database value to SQL NULL).
  3) description present with an empty string ("") means: store an empty string (not NULL).
- The frontend must implement a user-visible “clear” action that submits JSON null for description.
- The description string upper limit is 255 characters; this constraint is continuous and must be enforced/validated.
- The system must not automatically convert a missing/omitted description to null, and must not collapse an explicit empty string to null.
- Creation (POST) rules are unchanged and must not be altered by this update-flow work.

Frontend-specific implementation instructions:
1) Request composition rules for PUT updates:
   - If the user did not change the description field in the edit UI, do NOT include the description property in the JSON body at all.
   - If the user explicitly clears the description in the UI (using the provided “clear” control), include the description property with the JSON value null.
   - If the user explicitly sets the description to an empty string, include the description property with the JSON value "".
   - If the user enters a non-empty description, include the description property with that string (subject to length validation below).
   - Ensure the PUT request uses application/json and that your JSON serializer/transmitter does not drop properties whose value is null. If your default serializer strips null fields, configure or override it for this request so null is sent as JSON null.

2) Client-side validation and UX:
   - Enforce a maximum length of 255 characters for description input. Prevent submission when the entered string length > 255 and show a clear validation error.
   - Do NOT perform any automatic conversion of an omitted/untouched description to null before sending.
   - Do NOT convert an explicit empty-string input to null anywhere in the client stack.
   - The “clear” control must be unambiguous to the user and must cause the client to include description: null in the outgoing JSON body.
   - Preserve existing creation (POST) UI/behavior; do not change how description is handled at creation.

3) Implementation notes and pitfalls to avoid:
   - If your HTTP client or JSON library strips null-valued properties by default, explicitly configure it to include nulls for the update payload or construct the JSON body manually for the description field when null is required.
   - If you use a UI data model that auto-initializes fields (e.g., defaulting to empty string), ensure you can distinguish between "untouched (omit)" and "explicit empty string." One safe approach: track whether the user touched/edited the description field; only include description in the outgoing JSON if touched OR if the user used the clear action.
   - Do not change server-side creation behavior from the client side.

4) Acceptance test cases to implement on the frontend (each should be runnable and assert server-side state per backend acceptance):
   - Case A (omit): Open entry edit, do not change description, send PUT -> request body must NOT include description property; server should leave description unchanged.
   - Case B (null): Use “clear” control, send PUT -> request body must include "description": null; server should set description to NULL.
   - Case C (empty string): Set description input to "" explicitly, send PUT -> request body must include "description": ""; server should set description to empty string.
   - Case D (valid string): Set description to non-empty string of length <=255, send PUT -> request body includes that string; server should save it.
   - Case E (too long): Enter description of length >255, block submission client-side and show validation error; do not send PUT.

Frontend omissions (explicit):
- Omitted backend/internal storage implementation details (database schema, SQL statements) are out of scope for the frontend; frontend will only implement the request semantics described above and client-side validation. The exact server response codes/messages are not assumed here; the frontend should surface validation errors returned by the server per existing project conventions."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts (repeat):
- When receiving a PUT to update an entry, the description field has three distinct meanings:
  1) description omitted (field absent from the JSON) means: do NOT modify the stored description.
  2) description present with JSON null means: clear the stored description (store SQL NULL).
  3) description present with an empty string ("") means: store an empty string, not NULL.
- The frontend will implement a user-visible “clear” action that submits JSON null for description.
- The description string upper limit is 255 characters; this constraint is continuous and must be enforced/validated on the backend as well.
- The system must not automatically convert a missing/omitted description to NULL, and must not collapse an explicit empty string to NULL.
- Creation (POST) rules remain unchanged and must not be altered here.

Backend-specific implementation instructions:
1) Request parsing & semantics:
   - Parse the incoming PUT JSON body and detect whether the description key is present in the parsed object. Distinguish three cases:
     a) Key absent: do not change the existing description value for that record.
     b) Key present with value null: update the record so the description column is set to SQL NULL.
     c) Key present with a string value (including empty string): validate and set the description column to that exact string value.
   - Ensure your JSON body parser does not discard null-valued keys before your handler logic runs. If your framework strips nulls by default, configure it or access the raw input so you can tell the difference between 'absent' and 'present:null'.

2) Validation rules:
   - If description is present and is a string, enforce maximum length 255. If it exceeds 255, reject the update with a validation error (a client error response per existing project conventions) and do not modify the stored data.
   - If description is null, skip length validation (null means clear).
   - If description key is absent, skip validation for description because it is not being modified.

3) Data persistence behavior:
   - When performing the update, do not perform a blind full-field replace that treats missing fields as NULL. Only update description when the key is present. Implement the update statement so that description is included in the SET clause only when the description key was present in the request. Examples:
     - If key absent: UPDATE ... SET other_field = ... WHERE id = ... (no change to description column)
     - If key present & null: UPDATE ... SET description = NULL, ... WHERE id = ...
     - If key present & string: UPDATE ... SET description = '<string>', ... WHERE id = ...
   - Be cautious with ORMs that map absent properties to null during model binding; ensure your ORM layer distinguishes absent vs present-null vs present-string.

4) Tests the backend must implement (mirror frontend acceptance cases):
   - Case A (omit): Send PUT without description property -> verify stored description unchanged.
   - Case B (null): Send PUT with "description": null -> verify stored description becomes SQL NULL.
   - Case C (empty string): Send PUT with "description": "" -> verify stored description becomes an empty string.
   - Case D (valid string): Send PUT with a string of length <=255 -> verify stored description set to that string.
   - Case E (too long): Send PUT with string length >255 -> verify response is a validation error and stored description unchanged.

5) Error/response handling guidance (do not invent project-wide conventions):
   - On validation failure for description (length >255) return a client error with a clear validation message; pick the exact status code/format consistent with existing project conventions (do not change creation/posting conventions).

Backend omissions (explicit):
- Omitted frontend UI specifics: how the user triggers the clear action, or how the client tracks touched/untouched fields, is outside backend scope. The backend assumes the client will send requests exactly per the above JSON semantics.
- Omitted any assumptions about endpoint URLs, authentication, or global response-format conventions beyond validating and rejecting invalid description input per existing project conventions."
  }
}
